questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take lines to lines and segments to segments of the same length
questions.prompt: Segment AB has endpoints A(1, 2) and B(5, 2). It is translated 3 units down. What are the endpoints of the image, and how long is the image?
questions.prompt_markup:
Segment AB has endpoints A(1, 2) and B(5, 2). It is translated 3 units down.
What are the endpoints of the image, and how long is the image?
questions.correct_answer: A'(1, -1) and B'(5, -1); it is 4 units long, the same as AB.
questions.grading_note: Grade both the endpoints and the length.

questions.skill: Verify that rigid motions take lines to lines and segments to segments of the same length
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Reflect segment AB across the y-axis. Draw the image A'B'. Then find the lengths of AB and A'B' and compare them.
questions.prompt_markup: Reflect segment AB across the y-axis. Draw the image A'B'. Then find the lengths of AB and A'B' and compare them.
questions.correct_answer: AB = A'B' = √13 units (about 3.6 units); the reflection kept the length.
questions.drawing_answer: The segment from A'(-1, 1) to B'(-4, 3)
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the image segment, and the two equal lengths found from the grid (run 3, rise 2).

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from -6 to 6 and y from -6 to 6. Points: A (1, 1), B (4, 3). Straight line through (1, 1) and (4, 3).

sections.skill: Define rotations, reflections, and translations precisely

questions.skill: Define rotations, reflections, and translations precisely
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A reflection across line m maps a point P that is not on m to the point P'. How is line m related to segment PP'?
questions.prompt_markup:
A reflection across line m maps a point P that is not on m to the point P'.
How is line m related to segment PP'?
questions.correct_answer: Line m is the perpendicular bisector of PP'.

questions.prompt_markup:
A rotation of 90° about point O maps a point P (P ≠ O) to P'.
What is true about OP, OP', and angle POP'?
questions.correct_answer: OP = OP', and angle POP' measures 90°.

sections.skill: Use rigid motions to decide whether figures are congruent

questions.skill: Use rigid motions to decide whether figures are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is mapped onto triangle DEF by a rotation followed by a translation. What can you conclude about the triangles?
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangle ABC is mapped onto triangle DEF by a rotation followed by a translation.
What can you conclude about the triangles?
questions.correct_answer: They are congruent; their corresponding sides and angles are equal.

questions.skill: Use rigid motions to decide whether figures are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Explain why two figures are congruent when a sequence of rigid motions maps one onto the other.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why two figures are congruent when a sequence of rigid motions maps one onto the other.
questions.correct_answer: Rigid motions keep all lengths and angle measures, so every part of one figure matches the corresponding part of the other.
